subtitle: When Two River Kingdoms Met on the Eastern Edge of India

panels.shot: wide aerial over braided rivers and misty valleys
panels.action: Kalyanavarman of Kamarupa stands on a rocky ridge above the Brahmaputra valley, cloak stirred by wind, as distant smaller rivers and a faint, separate townscape in the Kopili-Kolong basin hint at another kingdom beyond.

dialogue.text: In the mist between the Brahmaputra and the sea, two river realms—Kamarupa and Davaka—rose side by side; the record names them both, but only one will remain.

i18n.hi: ब्रह्मपुत्र और सागर के धुंधले बीच, दो नदी राज्य–कामरूप और दावक–साथ उठे; लेखों ने दोनों के नाम लिखे, पर टिकेगा बस एक ही।

panels.shot: tight focus on the carved surface of the Allahabad Pillar, low-angle
panels.action: The weathered stone of the Allahabad Pillar fills the frame, delicate Gupta-era carvings and faint lines of script catching slanting light, while the sprawling Ganga plain blurs in the background.

dialogue.text: On the Ganga plain, Samudragupta’s pillar cut the frontier into stone, listing Kamarupa and Davaka as separate names on India’s eastern edge.

i18n.hi: गंगा समतल पर समुद्रगुप्त का स्तंभ सीमा पर नक़्श बन गया, जहाँ कामरूप और दावक अलग नामों से भारत के पूरब किनारे पर दर्ज हुए।

panels.shot: map-like overhead of eastern India, with rivers glowing faintly
panels.action: A stylised parchment map shows the Ganga to the west and the great eastward curve of the Brahmaputra; two shaded regions, one along the main river marked Kamarupa, another in the Kopili-Kolong basin marked Davaka, are linked by winding waterways.

dialogue.text: To the north-east lay Kamarupa on the Brahmaputra; to its south, in the Kopili-Kolong valleys, Davaka held fields, forests and river roads of its own.

i18n.hi: उत्तरोपूर्व में ब्रह्मपुत्र किनारे कामरूप था; उसके दक्षिण, कोपिली‑कोलोंग घाटियों में दावक ने अपनी खेत, जंगल और नदी‑राहें साध रखीं।

panels.shot: broad landscape wide of Kopili-Kolong valley at dawn
panels.action: Morning mist lifts over lush paddy terraces in the Kopili-Kolong basin, smoke from village hearths rising among bamboo groves; narrow boats move along a calm river that snakes between low hills.

dialogue.text: Here in Davaka’s heart, smaller rivers fed wet-rice fields and clustered settlements, tying hill, plain and water into one woven landscape.

i18n.hi: यहीं दावक के दिल में, छोटी नदियाँ धान के खेतों और गाँवों को सींचतीं, पहाड़, मैदान और जल को एक बुना हुआ संसार बना देतीं।

panels.shot: medium interior of a modest but ordered royal court
panels.action: Inside a wooden-pillared hall with thatched roof and carved beams, Kalyanavarman sits alert on a simple throne, palm-leaf records stacked beside him, while a courtier unrolls a map marked with rivers and villages.

dialogue.text: Far upstream, Kamarupa’s ruler Kalyanavarman watched his frontier grow, learning that to rule this land, one must first understand its rivers.

i18n.hi: बहुत ऊपर, कामरूप का नरेश कल्याणवर्मन अपनी बढ़ती सीमा देखता, सीखता कि इस देश को चलाना हो तो पहले नदियों को समझना होगा।

panels.shot: low wide shot of a trade boat on a broad river
panels.action: A long wooden boat heavy with sacks of grain and jars of oil glides down a wide river, oarsmen straining in rhythm while small waystations on the bank watch their passing.

dialogue.text: Boats carried more than goods; they carried news, tribute and the first threads of alliance, binding Kamarupa’s Brahmaputra to Davaka’s tributary world.

i18n.hi: नावें केवल माल नहीं, खबरें, नज़राने और पहली दोस्ती की डोरें भी ढोतीं, ब्रह्मपुत्र की धारा को दावक की सहायक नदियों से बाँध देतीं।

panels.shot: intimate interior in a Davaka court, three-quarter view
panels.action: In another hall built of timber and thatch, a Davaka ruler in simple ornaments listens as a scribe points to a palm-leaf scroll bearing foreign characters, a faint sense of the wider world painted on his thoughtful face.

dialogue.text: Davaka was no mythic province; it was a court with its own scribes, countryside and choices, facing both upland chiefs and distant empires.

i18n.hi: दावक कोई कल्पित सूबा नहीं था; वह अपना दरबार, लेखक, देहात और फैसलों वाला राज्य था, सामने पहाड़ी सरदार भी थे और दूर‑दूर के साम्राज्य भी।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of a coastal or riverine port with ships preparing
panels.action: A busy river-port scene shows carpenters hammering on a larger vessel while craftsmen load fine cloth and ivory; a small delegation in eastern attire boards, banners furled, preparing for a long voyage.

dialogue.text: In 428, Chinese records tell of an embassy from Kapili—Davaka’s realm—sailing east with gifts and petitions to the Liu Song court.

i18n.hi: सन् 428 में, चीनी लेखों में कपिली—दावक का देश—का दूतमंडल दर्ज है, जो पूर्व की ओर लियू सोंग दरबार तक तोहफ़े और अर्ज़ियाँ लेकर गया।

panels.shot: formal interior in a Chinese palace hall, symmetric frontal
panels.action: Within a grand Chinese hall with high roof and lacquered pillars, Song dynasty officials stand in ordered rows as a modestly dressed embassy from the south-east bows, presenting lacquered boxes on a long tray.

dialogue.text: There, amid lacquered beams and silk robes, Davaka appeared in foreign annals as an independent voice from the distant riverlands of India.

i18n.hi: वहाँ, सजी हुई छतों और रेशमी वस्त्रों के बीच, दावक विदेशी इतिहासों में दूरस्थ भारतीय नदी‑देश की एक स्वतंत्र आवाज़ बनकर उभरा।

panels.shot: close-up on Kalyanavarman’s profile over a map, side lighting
panels.action: By lamplight, Kalyanavarman leans over a palm-leaf map etched with the Brahmaputra and its tributaries, his finger resting on the Kopili-Kolong confluence, eyes narrowed in deliberation.

dialogue.text: By the 420s, his attention turned downstream, to where Davaka’s valleys touched the great river, a hinge between interior and sea.

i18n.hi: 420 के दशक तक, उसकी नज़र अब धारा की ओर झुकी, जहाँ दावक की घाटियाँ महान नदी से जुड़ती थीं—भीतर और सागर के बीच की एक कड़ी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kalyanavarman with advisors in council
panels.action: In the Kamarupa court, Kalyanavarman hears two advisors: one pointing towards a clay model of a river junction, another holding a bundle of tied paddy stalks, while guards stand quietly behind.

dialogue.speaker: kalyanavarman_and_davaka
dialogue.text: If we hold the tributaries, we hold the harvest and the boats.

i18n.hi: अगर सहायक नदियाँ हमारे हाथ हैं, तो फ़सल और नावें भी हमारी हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kopili-Kolong confluence, semi-aerial
panels.action: From above, two shining tributaries merge towards the broader Brahmaputra, their banks lined with scattered hamlets, ferry ghats and small shrines under spreading trees.

dialogue.text: The Kopili and Kolong were more than streams; they were corridors of grain and people, the routes by which Kamarupa could become a true Brahmaputra kingdom.

i18n.hi: कोपिली और कोलोंग महज़ धाराएँ नहीं थीं; वे अन्न और लोगों के गलियारे थे, जिनसे कामरूप सचमुच ब्रह्मपुत्र का राज्य बन सकता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of rural chiefs and envoys in a village meeting
panels.action: In a village clearing, local headmen in simple wraps sit in a circle with two differently dressed envoys, one bearing Kamarupa’s emblem, another with Davaka’s style, in a tense yet measured gathering.

dialogue.text: Later scholars see these years as a time when allegiances shifted—villages, chiefs and routes moving gradually under Kalyanavarman’s orbit.

i18n.hi: बाद के विद्वान इन वर्षों को वफ़ादारियों के बदलने का समय मानते हैं—गाँव, सरदार और राहें धीरे‑धीरे कल्याणवर्मन के घेरे में खिसकती गईं।

panels.shot: wide of a riverine fort or administrative post under construction
panels.action: Workers stack timber and earth to shape a small riverside fort, while officials oversee the work and villagers bring baskets of soil; the river glints beside this new outpost.

dialogue.text: Without a recorded great battle, the change left other traces: new posts on the rivers, new collectors, new routes of tribute and order.

i18n.hi: बड़ी लड़ाई का कोई लेख नहीं, पर बदलती हवा और निशान दिखे: नदियों पर नए ठिकाने, नए वसूलीकार, नज़राने और हुक्म की नई राहें।

panels.shot: slow zoom-out from a palm-leaf chronicle with empty space
panels.action: A hand carefully writes on a palm leaf, then the view pulls back to show blank, unwritten leaves beyond, a subtle gap between what is inscribed and what remains empty.

dialogue.text: Yet the process itself is lost to silence; no inscription survives to tell how Davaka’s rulers yielded or were absorbed.

i18n.hi: पर यह पूरा दौर ख़ामोशी में खो गया; कोई लेख नहीं बताता कि दावक के शासक कैसे झुके या समा लिए गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kalyanavarman in later years by the river
panels.action: An older Kalyanavarman stands by the Brahmaputra at dusk, watching barges glide past loaded with grain, his expression inward, the sky painted in muted oranges.

dialogue.text: What we do know is that under his reign, Kamarupa’s reach spread over the central Brahmaputra, drawing the Kopili-Kolong basin into a single river polity.

i18n.hi: जानते बस इतना हैं कि उसके राज में कामरूप का हाथ मध्य ब्रह्मपुत्र तक फैल गया, कोपिली‑कोलोंग घाटी को एक ही नदी राज्य में खींच लाया।

panels.shot: composite map dissolve, Davaka label fading into Kamarupa
panels.action: On the parchment map, the separate shading of Davaka slowly merges into Kamarupa’s colour, its name becoming fainter until only Kamarupa remains over a larger swathe of valley and river.

dialogue.text: Davaka, once listed apart on Samudragupta’s pillar and in Chinese books, vanishes from later records as Kamarupa’s name covers the middle valley.

i18n.hi: दावक, जिसे समुद्रगुप्त के स्तंभ और चीनी ग्रंथों में अलग दर्ज किया गया था, बाद के लेखों से गुम हो जाता है, जब कामरूप का नाम पूरे मध्य घाटी पर छा जाता है।

panels.shot: modern-like aerial of the Brahmaputra valley, timeless feel
panels.action: A sweeping aerial view shows the wide Brahmaputra winding through central Assam, its sandbars, villages and fields stretching to the horizon, with smaller rivers feeding into it from wooded hills.

dialogue.text: In this landscape, power followed water: whoever held the tributary basins, wet-rice lands and boat routes could knit a frontier into a kingdom.

i18n.hi: इस धरती पर सत्ता जल के पीछे चलती थी: जो सहायक घाटियाँ, धान की ज़मीनें और नाव‑राहें पकड़ ले, वही सीमा को जोड़‑जोड़कर राज्य बना दे।

panels.shot: lingering close on the weathered Allahabad Pillar again, now with river in background
panels.action: The frame returns to the Allahabad Pillar rising against the sky, a distant river glinting behind it, the old inscriptions softened by age yet still legible in parts.

dialogue.text: Kalyanavarman’s Kamarupa endures in later chronicles; Davaka survives only in a pillar and a Chinese scroll, a reminder that rivers remember kingdoms even when chronicles forget them.

i18n.hi: कल्याणवर्मन का कामरूप आगे की कथाओं में बचा रहता है; दावक बस एक स्तंभ और एक चीनी पांडुलिपि में जिंदा है—याद दिलाता कि नदियाँ राजों को याद रखती हैं, चाहे इतिहास उन्हें भूल जाए।

title_i18n.hi: दावक ने ब्रह्मपुत्र लोक में कदम रखा

subtitle_i18n.en: When Two River Kingdoms Met on the Eastern Edge of India
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब दो नदी राज्य मिले, भारत के पूरब किनारे पर
